title: CONDA: Condensed Deep Association Learning for Co-Salient Object Detection

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Equation (17) defines the OCC loss L_s^C, but the immediately following text reads 'where (k_c, k_c) is the center position of K × K square.' This sentence belongs to the context of Equation (15) in Section 3.3 (Condensation Operation), not Equation (17). The correct explanatory text 'where G_i^s is the resized ground truth of image I_i' appears on the following line, indicating a copy-paste/editing artifact. This does not affect the mathematical correctness of Equation (17) itself.

The paper reports 'respective gains of 3.72%, 4.80%, 7.30%, and 1.31% in S_m, E_ξ, F_β, and M.' Since M (Mean Absolute Error) is a metric where lower values are better, describing a change as a 'gain' is ambiguous — it could mean either a percentage decrease (improvement) or a percentage increase (worsening). In computer vision literature, it is common to report all metric changes uniformly as 'gains' even for error metrics, implying the 'gain' for M is actually a reduction. Without the raw M values, this cannot be definitively classified as an error.

The paper writes '||·|| represents the l-2 norm' where the standard notation is 'L2 norm', 'ℓ2 norm', or 'Euclidean norm'. The lowercase 'l' is a typographical deviation from standard mathematical notation. This is a minor formatting issue with no impact on the mathematical content.

summary:
The paper 'CONDA: Condensed Deep Association Learning for Co-Salient Object Detection' was verified in exhaustive mode with lenient error sensitivity. Four specialist verifiers (math, text, cross-section consistency, and statistical) were applied to key snippets of the paper.

No critical errors were found that would warrant an erratum or correction. The paper's mathematical formulations are logically sound, the experimental design is consistent with the methodology, and there are no macro-level contradictions between sections (Abstract, Introduction, Methodology, Experiments, Conclusion).

Four minor issues were identified at low confidence levels: (1) a copy-paste text artifact after Equation (17) where explanatory text from an earlier equation was duplicated; (2) ambiguous reporting of the MAE metric change as a 'gain'; (3) a non-standard notation 'l-2 norm' instead of 'L2 norm'; and (4) minor grammar typos. None of these issues affects the paper's core scientific claims or conclusions.

The paper's contributions — deep association learning, progressive association generation (PAG), correspondence-induced association condensation (CAC), and object-aware cycle consistency (OCC) loss — are consistently described across all sections and supported by ablation studies and SOTA comparisons.
